reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a highly regular, piecewise-constant square-wave pattern with a fundamental period of approximately 98 points (consistent with the estimated period). Each cycle consists of a rapid upward step (~1–2 points), a flat high plateau lasting ~30–40 points, a rapid downward step (~1–2 points), and a flat low plateau lasting ~50–60 points. The waveform is stable across candidates: amplitude (peak-to-trough) ranges from ~1.3 to ~2.7 robust-standardized units, with median levels shifting modestly between candidates (−0.67 to +0.67), reflecting baseline drift rather than structural change. Peaks are sharp, symmetric, and consistently rectangular; troughs are similarly flat and well-defined. Noise is negligible—no visible jitter or stochastic variation within plateaus. Roughness and curvature metrics near zero confirm near-perfect step transitions. Minor morphological variations include occasional single-point overshoots (e.g., candidate 1 at index 1017, candidate 2 at 1847) and slight asymmetry in plateau durations, but the core 4-phase cycle repeats reliably. Acceptable variation includes ±0.3 in median level, ±0.3 in amplitude, and ±5 points in plateau length—within these bounds, deviations are likely due to robust standardization offsets or minor sensor quantization, not anomalies.

When query exhibits an isolated spike resembling candidate 2’s overshoot, compare against candidate 3’s clean cycles first before labeling anomalous.
